title: robotindex Product Record
description: Canonical record for one product in the robotindex directory. One file per product under data/products/<id>.json. The live HTML page for a product is rendered from this record, not hand-authored separately.

$schema.description: Editor/tooling hint pointing back at this schema file. Not semantically meaningful.

id.description: Stable unique id, kebab-case. Never reused, never renamed once published — other records and tooling reference a product by this id, not by its slug or name.

slug.description: Extensionless page path, e.g. 'product-unitree-go2' — this is the site's canonical URL form (see netlify.toml's redirects and every canonical/og:url tag). The generated file on disk is still <slug>.html; strip or add that suffix at the point a filename vs. a URL is actually needed, but never store '.html' in this field itself, since every href, canonical tag, sitemap entry, and crosslink card is built directly from it. Kept separate from id so the URL can change (renames, restructuring) without breaking references that use id.

manufacturer.description: Company or project name, e.g. 'Unitree Robotics'.

category.description: Top-level directory category, e.g. 'Humanoid & General Purpose'.

tier.description: Stepped review status shown as the product-meta badge; matches today's directory.js tier field. 'under-review' = added under 30 days ago, or availability still unconfirmed. 'new' = 30+ days since add date, with availability confirmed — promotion is rule-based (see the post-date field, once added). 'featured' is always a manual editorial call, never automatic. Distinct from flags.pending: a shipped, long-available product can still be tier=new if it just cleared the 30-day window, and flags.pending can be true on a tier=new record if the 30-day clock ran out before availability was reconfirmed — that combination should be treated as a signal to recheck the record, not as a contradiction to silently resolve either way.

pending.description: Not yet released, or availability unconfirmed. Distinct from tier: a shipped product can still be tier=pending due to thin sourcing.

openSource.description: True only if this product itself (hardware and/or software) qualifies under robotindex's Strict Open Source policy. Must agree with whether firmwareCommunity references an 'opensource' entry in builds-mods.json — these two must not be set independently by hand, or they drift the way the site's data did before this schema existed.

closedPlatform.description: True if the manufacturer has released no public SDK, firmware repo, or developer API. Drives the 'Closed platform' Firmware & Community message.

description.description: Short 1-3 sentence summary shown under the product name (today's .product-desc).

specs.description: Ordered list of spec cards. Deliberately NOT a fixed field set — a drone, a vacuum, and a robot arm share almost no spec names in practice (checked across the live pages: 'Suction'/'Mopping' for vacuums, 'Cutting Width'/'Max Slope' for mowers, 'Degrees of Freedom'/'Repeatability' for arms, 'Height'/'Hand DOF' for humanoids). Forcing one schema of named fields across categories would either lose real data or invent empty fields. Label/value/note as free text, ordered for display, is the closest structured form that doesn't lose information.

note.description: Secondary clarifying text shown smaller underneath (today's <small> tag), e.g. 'HyperForce digital motor'.

summary.description: Prose price statement shown under the 'Reference Price' heading.

tiers.description: Present only for products sold in multiple tiers (e.g. Go2 Air/Pro/X/EDU). Omit entirely for single-price or no-price products.

editorial.description: Long-form narrative sections beyond specs/pricing (today's freeform 'Sensors & Hardware', 'X — Worth Knowing', 'Generation Comparison', etc. headings, which vary per product and shouldn't be forced into one taxonomy). Body is markdown. This is intentionally the one place the schema stays loose — it's editorial voice, not data, and structuring it further would just be re-inventing prose as fields.

firmwareCommunity.description: Links into builds-mods.json by id, OR an explanation for why there isn't one. This is the field that was hand-duplicated (name + desc copy-pasted onto the product page AND into builds-mods.html's arrays) and drifted out of sync twice in one audit. Referencing by id instead of copying text makes that class of bug structurally impossible: there is exactly one place a repo's name/desc live.

buildsModsId.description: id of an entry in data/builds-mods.json.

status.description: closed-platform: no public SDK/firmware/API at all. unlicensed: a real repo exists but has no stated open license, so it doesn't qualify for builds-mods.json. not-listed: repo qualifies but hasn't been added yet.

note.description: The explanatory sentence shown in place of a link, e.g. 'Tesla has not released a public SDK...'.

sourcing.description: The citation/caveat text shown at the bottom of the page (today's .verify-note) — where the specs above came from and what couldn't be confirmed. Required on every record: this is what lets a developer building on this data trust it, or know exactly how much to trust it.
